messages:
ashley: heads up, trying to follow quickstart on a Windows laptop (WSL2 Ubuntu). installed redwoodctl via the MSI and the deb package in WSL, but `redwoodctl version` shows 0.9.3 in powershell and command not found in WSL.
ashley: when i run `redwoodctl login --profile work` in WSL it prints 'login complete' but my web app still gets 403 when using the SDK with the same profile.
reena: MSI vs deb path confusion. MSI puts binary in C:\\Program Files\\Redwood\\bin while WSL uses /usr/local/bin. You need to install inside WSL for the linux binary or use the Windows binary from powershell.
ashley: i installed in WSL with `sudo dpkg -i redwoodctl_0.9.3_amd64.deb` and then did `redwoodctl login` inside WSL. config file at ~/.redwood/config has two profiles: work and default. default.token shows "expired" in the file? not sure how that got there.
tom: can you paste `cat ~/.redwood/config` (redact tokens)? maybe the CLI wrote a refresh token but the SDK is using the default profile.
ashley: pasted snippet: 
profiles:
  work:
    token: "(redacted)"
    expires_at: "2026-11-01T12:00:00Z"
  default:
    token: "(redacted-old)"
    expires_at: "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"

ashley: the web app uses env REDWOOD_PROFILE=default (legacy). i updated it to work and restarted, still 403.
reena: is your SDK pinned to a version that expects token in `~/.redwood/credentials` instead of `~/.redwood/config`? we had an SDK parity issue where older SDKs looked up credentials differently.
ashley: good call. package.json shows "@redwood/sdk": "^0.8.0" in the sample app. i guess that's old.
tom: try upgrading SDK to latest or point the SDK explicitly to the config file with REDWOOD_CONFIG_PATH. Also `redwoodctl auth refresh --profile work` should force refresh and print new expiry.
ashley: `redwoodctl auth refresh --profile work` returned: "ok: token refreshed, expires_at=2026-11-01T12:00:00Z" but web app still 403.
infra-bot: note: there was a transient auth API throttling incident earlier today (INC-2026) which caused some refreshes to fail with 429; retries should help. see internal statuspage: https://status.redwood.company/incidents/2026
reena: can you run `REDWOOD_DEBUG=1 node ./scripts/start.js` in the app and paste the auth header seen by the SDK? masked of course. want to confirm it's sending the work token.
ashley: debug log shows header Authorization: Bearer (redacted-starts-with-abc123). config work token actually starts with abc123, so SDK is using work.
ashley: i noticed the SDK prints a deprecation warning: "credential lookup: ~/.redwood/credentials is deprecated, please use ~/.redwood/config". but the app still errors.
tom: there's one more thing: some deployments treat tokens created by CLI v0.9.3 as ephemeral unless a client_id is present in the profile. newer redwoodctl includes client_id in the profile; older installers didn't. run `redwoodctl login --profile work --client-id local-dev` to regenerate with client id.
ashley: did that, login flow completed and config now shows client_id: "local-dev" under work. restarted app -> still 403.
ashley: stacktrace from app: "403 Forbidden: invalid_token: token signature invalid"
reena: signature invalid suggests token hammered by a different signing key or you're hitting the hosted API but using a private deployment audience. double-check REDWOOD_API_HOST in app.env. if it's pointing to staging-private.redwood.company while token audience is hosted, you'll get signature mismatch.
ashley: omg yes my .env in WSL had REDWOOD_API_HOST=https://staging-private.redwood.company from previous testing. i changed it to https://api.redwood.company and restarted -> auth works. app got 200.
ashley: summary: multiple layers here: 1) install mismatch between Windows MSI and WSL deb, 2) old SDK expecting different credential file, 3) need client_id for some token flows, 4) ensure REDWOOD_API_HOST matches token audience.
reena: thanks for the writeup. i'll add a small blurb to the quickstart on WSL vs Windows installs and a note about REDWOOD_PROFILE and REDWOOD_API_HOST.
infra-bot: opened INF-4799: quickstart: clarify installer differences (MSI vs deb) and add troubleshooting section for WSL.
devex-bot: internal guide: https://redwood.company/docs/devex/cli-wsl-install + link to INF-4799
ashley: thanks all. one last ask: is there a way to list active profiles quickly? i had to open the file to check.
reena: `redwoodctl profile list` shows profiles and expiry in human-readable form in latest CLI. if your version doesn't have it, upgrade to 0.9.6.
ashley: `redwoodctl profile list` worked after upgrade. closing this thread. :white_check_mark:
